chapter: Playing bass in the early bands
title: Roles in the ensemble: clarinet, ensemble and the Night Owls
summary: He explains each instrument's role, with Ferguson's Pee Wee Spitelera story and the band's ensemble approach.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: What kind of a part did the clarinet play?
The clarinet player always did play the variations. I'll admit I did. But they do learn? They tried to fill in as much as they possibly could.

Can I digress for a moment, Bill, on this very point, getting kind of modern now. When Pete Fountain was Al Hurt's clarinet player and then he went out and got on Lawrence Welk and so on. He really never did come back to the band. And Pee Wee Spadalera went into Al Hurt's band. And I was walking down Bourbon Street to buy my paper, as I do many a night, and I ran into Pee Wee standing on the corner outside the club down there. And he had been with Al about two weeks at that time. I said, Pee Wee, how do you like playing with Al Hurt? And he said, well I really don't know what to play. And of course he was a very capable clarinet player and I wasn't expecting any answer like that. And I said, well what do you mean you don't know what to play? And he said, Al plays all of his notes and then he plays all of mine. Yep.

You see, the idea of making a band and having a band like that, is for a band to play together. That's what makes a band. It don't have to be ex-boys and stars. As long as they play together. It's just like you take a football team or a baseball team. They got to work together and they got to play together. If one of them is going to show more than they can show the rest of them what he can do and what he can do, then you break up the team. Well that's the same thing with music. If the trumpet player is going to play a lead, play a lead. You know the clarinet player plays the variations, play the variations. The trombone plays the trombone parts, he knows. That's the counter melody of the music. You understand what I mean? Don't try to play with the trumpet is playing or try to play with the clarinet is playing. You understand that? That's the thing that makes a band. But that's what plenty of these bands can understand.

That's one reason, Chink, the band you're playing in now is called the Night Owls, because we want ensemble. We think that if you start out with so-and-so and his orchestra, right away you've lost the ensemble because it's a showcase for one man.
Fifty years ago did they have a lot of solos? They start out an ensemble and everybody plays the same.
